correctness.rationale: The stationary law is a geometrically aged beta-binomial urn: regenerate at rate r, conditional variance k/[4(n+1)(n+k)], conditional martingale identity gives covariance (1-r)^h Var(X). The de Finetti representation supplies the Gaussian weak- and intermediate-reset regimes; for nr→∞, jumps of scaled martingales are ≤sqrt(r), predictable bracket →t/4, Bernoulli reset epochs converge to unit-rate Poisson, giving the stationary J1 Brownian-reset process with generator f''/8+f(0)-f. Ages scaled by r converge to Exp(1) and its Gaussian variance mixture is Laplace of characteristic function (1+s²/8)^−1. Even n, balanced deterministic resets, r→0 and compact finite horizons are essential. Independently recalculated conditional beta-binomial second moments; fixed-n tests do not establish functional convergence.
residual_risks: Functional J1 concatenation and stationary episode tightness rely on standard FCLT and tightness conditions; finite second-moment check does not establish them.
